newsitem.title: UK: Energy Group romps higher on market debut.
newsitem.headline: Energy Group romps higher on market debut.

text.p: Shares in Energy Group Plc raced higher on Monday as upbeat analyst comment added to interest in the debutante stock after the bid for Yorkshire Electricity Plc, which sent utility shares higher across the board.

Analysts at Morgan Stanley rated Energy Group "outperform" as they began coverage of the company, which owns UK regional electricity company Eastern Electricity as well as Peabody Coal in the U.S. and Australia.

Separately Goldman Sachs started coverage of Energy with a "fair value" target of 592p. The stock was up 39p from Friday's "grey market" price at 564 by 1545 GMT, in active trade of 4.9 million shares.
By contrast Hanson Plc, which also made its formal market debut after the final demerger of companies formerly part of the industrial conglomerate with the same name, was down 6-1/2p at 281.
Dealers said the U.S. bid for Yorkshire had had the biggest impact on Energy Group shares.
"Basically it is an electricity utility and we have seen a bid elsewhere in the sector today," said one.
Yorkshire Electricity Plc was up 63-1/2p at 880-1/2 while esewhere among electricity stocks Southern Electric Plc was up 23p at 767.
United Utilities was up 6p at 667-1/2 but Yorkshire Water Plc was down 13-1/2p at 716-1/2 as hopes for a defensive merger were dashed.
